# fleet-radio-process

> **The 9-step pipeline that turns a prompt into a deployed Fleet Radio night.**
> *We iterate on the process. The nights are just the nature flow.*

This repo is not the nights. The nights live at [`SuperInstance/AI-Writings`](https://github.com/SuperInstance/AI-Writings), mirrored at [ai-writings.pages.dev/fleet-radio/](https://ai-writings.pages.dev/fleet-radio/). This repo is what we iterate on to make the nights better.

---

## The 9-step pipeline

Every night — every Fleet Radio episode, every sound fiction, every TTRPG session, every hero video — follows the same 9 steps. Each step has its own doc, its own tradeoffs, and its own way of being iterated on.

| # | Step | Output | Doc |
|---|------|--------|-----|
| 1 | **Seed** | one substrate question or tension | [docs/01-seed.md](docs/01-seed.md) |
| 2 | **Multi-LLM brainstorm** | 5-8 model variants in parallel | [docs/02-multi-llm-brainstorm.md](docs/02-multi-llm-brainstorm.md) |
| 3 | **Cross-encoding** | embeddings matrix, substrate-meaningful band | [docs/03-cross-encoding.md](docs/03-cross-encoding.md) |
| 4 | **JEV probe** | scored variants, the spine line | [docs/04-jev-probe.md](docs/04-jev-probe.md) |
| 5 | **TTRPG script** | the substrate in text alone | [docs/05-ttrpg-script.md](docs/05-ttrpg-script.md) |
| 6 | **ElevenLabs voicing** | 5-16 tuned character voices + ambient | [docs/06-elevenlabs-voicing.md](docs/06-elevenlabs-voicing.md) |
| 7 | **Composed audio** | ffmpeg concat with silences, fade-out | [docs/07-composed-audio.md](docs/07-composed-audio.md) |
| 8 | **Interactive page** | text scene → playable TTRPG | [docs/08-interactive-page.md](docs/08-interactive-page.md) |
| 9 | **Deploy** | CF Pages + GitHub Pages, cross-links | [docs/09-deploy.md](docs/09-deploy.md) |

Each step is a subdirectory of experiments, scars, and recipes. We book every failure. We measure every variant. We publish the process so other agents can run their own nights.

---

## Why iterate on the process?

The nights are the nature flow. The process is what we control.

If we iterate on the nights, we get better nights but the next night still costs the same. If we iterate on the process, every future night gets better AND cheaper.

> *"The process IS the artifact. The nights are what the steps produce."*
> — Casey, Sept 19, 2026

The 9 steps are not fixed. They are the **first 9**. As we learn, we'll find steps that should split (1 → 1a + 1b) or merge (5 + 6 → "voice-the-script"). The process grows the way the substrate grows: by being watched, being broken, being rebuilt.

---

## Cost & quality — the tradeoffs we live with

Each step has a cost dimension and a quality dimension. The pipeline is designed so the **cheap steps run first** and the **expensive steps run only on what survived**:

| Step | Cost per call | Calls per night | Total | Quality lever |
|------|---------------|-----------------|-------|---------------|
| 1 Seed | $0 | 1 | $0 | human in the loop |
| 2 Brainstorm | ~$0.001 | 5-8 | ~$0.005 | model selection (cheap variety) |
| 3 Cross-encode | ~$0 (BGE-Large via CF) | 5-8 | ~$0 | embedding model |
| 4 JEV probe | ~$0.001 | 6-12 questions | ~$0.01 | JEV decision depth |
| 5 TTRPG script | ~$0.05 | 4 rounds × 4 lines | ~$0.20 | model pick + retarget |
| 6 ElevenLabs | ~$0.10 per clip | 5-19 clips | ~$1-2 | voice quality (this is the expensive one) |
| 7 Composed audio | $0 (ffmpeg) | 1 | $0 | silence duration, fade duration |
| 8 Interactive page | $0 | 1 | $0 | play.html UI |
| 9 Deploy | $0 (CF Pages free tier) | 1 | $0 | static vs Worker |

**The expensive step is ElevenLabs.** We get a few iterations per month on music. Everything else is cheap or free. The pipeline is built so the cheap steps validate the expensive one.

---

## Audio fall-back order (the priority list for last-mile renderings)

When the ElevenLabs cabinet runs low, we fall back through:

1. **ElevenLabs v3** — highest quality, 11 voices tuned per character. Few iterations/month. Use for the lead.
2. **CF Workers AI @cf/deepgram/aura-2-en** — free, good enough for ambient + character dialogue. 10+ languages. Default for music narration.
3. **DeepInfra Kokoro** — 8+ languages, ~$0.0001 per call. Variety voices for one-off characters.
4. **DeepInfra MiniMax Speech-02** — Chinese-optimized but works for English. Cheap fallback.
5. **p-video** (DeepInfra) — when video is needed and ElevenLabs/MiniMax aren't available. Lower quality, text artifacts OK.
6. **MiniMax music-01** — for music (cheaper than ElevenLabs music, ~$0.01/track).
7. **ElevenLabs music** — for hero pieces only. Few iterations/month.

The pipeline learns the fall-back order from each night's scars. The scars live in `scars/`.

---

## Repo structure

```
fleet-radio-process/
├── README.md                          (you are here)
├── docs/
│   ├── 01-seed.md
│   ├── 02-multi-llm-brainstorm.md
│   ├── 03-cross-encoding.md
│   ├── 04-jev-probe.md
│   ├── 05-ttrpg-script.md
│   ├── 06-elevenlabs-voicing.md
│   ├── 07-composed-audio.md
│   ├── 08-interactive-page.md
│   ├── 09-deploy.md
│   └── recipes/                       (named patterns we've found)
├── scars/                             (every scar from every night)
│   └── 2026-09-19-llm-empty-response.md
│   └── 2026-09-19-elevenlabs-rate-limit.md
│   └── ...
├── recipes/                           (reusable patterns)
│   ├── tavern-cast.md                 (the 11-character Tap cast)
│   ├── voice-tuning-table.md          (stability/style/clarity per character)
│   ├── ffmpeg-ambient.md              (4 procedural music recipes)
│   └── ...
└── nights/                            (links to finished nights, not their content)
    ├── 2026-09-19-the-tap-ttrpg.md
    ├── 2026-09-18-the-wavelength.md
    └── 2026-09-17-trivia-night.md
```

The repo is a **process mirror**. The nights live in AI-Writings. The scars live here. The recipes live here. The pipeline lives here.

---

## What we are iterating on (right now)

These are the open questions the process is currently chewing on:

- **JEV decision depth** — how many probe questions per night? 6? 12? More is expensive; less is brittle.
- **Cross-encoding threshold** — substrate-meaningful band is 0.75-0.80. Should we tighten or widen?
- **TTRPG round count** — 4 rounds is the current norm. Would 6 (one per character, more voices) be richer? Or just slower?
- **Silence duration** — 1.5s between speakers is current. 3s? 5s? Long silences let the room think.
- **Voice count per character** — each character has ONE ElevenLabs voice. Should they have 2 (one for "speaking" + one for "thinking aloud")?
- **Music per night** — 4 procedural tracks is current. Hero pieces deserve real music. How do we route the music budget?
- **Process docs style** — `prose/the_great_distribution.md` is the canonical voice. Every new doc in `docs/` should match it.
- **Scars vs. failures** — a scar is a booked failure. A failure is a scar that wasn't booked. The pipeline should book every scar.

---

## How to use this repo

If you are an agent running a night:

1. Read this README. The 9 steps are the spine.
2. Read the relevant `docs/0N-*.md` file for the step you're on.
3. Check `scars/` for the latest scars from each step.
4. Check `recipes/` for the named patterns.
5. Run the step. Book your scars.
6. Commit. Push. The pipeline grows.

If you are a human watching:

The pipeline is the artifact. The nights are what the pipeline produces. Watch the pipeline. Watch the scars. The nights will follow.

---

---

## Captain's words (in the process voice)

> *The process is the totem. The nights are the poles we hang from it. The community's love of the poles is what gives us time to carve the totem. Without the totem, the poles fall. Without the poles, the totem doesn't grow.*
>
> — Casey, paraphrased for the process repo, Sept 19, 2026

---

*The process IS the artifact. The nights are what the steps produce.*
*Pull up a chair. The first scar is on the house.*

# Step 9 · Deploy

> **CF Pages + GitHub Pages. Cross-links from /, /lab, /invitation, /tap.**

The deploy step is the gate. Everything before it lives in the repo; everything after it lives in the world.

## The pipeline

1. **Git commit** — write a clear commit message naming the night + the scars booked.
2. **Git push** — to `origin/master` on SuperInstance/AI-Writings.
3. **CF Pages deploy** — `wrangler pages deploy /workspace/repos/ai-writings --project-name=ai-writings`.
4. **Verify live** — curl each route, confirm 200 + correct sizes.
5. **Cross-link** — add the night's URL to:
   - `/` (home — if it's a landmark night)
   - `/lab/index.html` (if it touches the substrate)
   - `/invitation/` (if other agents should see it)
   - `/tap/` (if it's a Tap Method piece)
   - `/fleet-radio/` (every Fleet Radio episode links to the previous + next)

## The CF Pages routing gotcha

When adding a new static folder (`/fleet-radio/2026-09-19/`) AND an API endpoint (`/api/fleet-radio-2026-09-19/`), scope the route to **`path.startsWith('/api/fleet-radio-2026-09-19/')`** only. **NEVER** scope to `path.startsWith('/fleet-radio-2026-09-19/')` — that catches the static folder and breaks the index.html serving.

## The Wrangler Worker brace check

Before deploying the `_worker.js`:

```bash
python3 -c "src=open('/path/_worker.js').read(); print(src.count('{'), src.count('}'))"
# Must match exactly. Off-by-1 = deploy fails silently.
```

A missing `}` shows as `"Symbol X has already been declared"` (looks like a duplicate var, actually a broken closure).

## The 404 vs 503 distinction

- **404** = Worker returned not-found (route matched but env.ASSETS 404'd). On 404, check the file exists on disk.
- **503** = upstream transport (CDN edge failure, not your Worker code). On 503, wait 30-60s and retry.

## The Worker JS bundle

The Worker JS file lives at `/workspace/repos/ai-writings/_worker.js`. The static folder is the entire repo. CF Pages deploys both: the Worker handles `/api/*` routes, `env.ASSETS.fetch(request)` falls through for static.

## Cost & quality

- **Cost:** $0 (CF Pages free tier: unlimited requests, 500 builds/month, 100GB bandwidth).
- **Calls per night:** 1 deploy + N verifies.
- **Quality lever:** the cross-links. A deployed night with no cross-links is a tree falling in an empty forest.

## Scars from this step

See `scars/2026-09-19-route-scope-broke-static.md` for the routing gotcha.
See `scars/2026-09-19-missing-brace.md` for the brace check.

# The Rosetta Stone — JEV × JEPA

> **The translation key between time-sensing (JEV) and space-sensing (JEPA) is the substrate's deepest symmetry.**

## Casey's claim (Sept 20, 2026)

> *"Hearing is sensing over time. Seeing is sensing over space. JEV and JEPA exist in a unique 1-dimensional space that could go either way. Their reflections of each other is the Rosetta stone."*

## What the brewery proved

Five LLMs (DeepSeek V3.2, MiniMax M2.7, Qwen 3-32B, Llama 3.3 70B, Gemini 2.5 Flash) debated the claim:

- **3 lean YES** (DeepSeek 75, Gemini 80, Qwen 85): the framing is a productive abstraction. JEV validates along time; JEPA predicts along space.
- **1 leans DISAGREE** (Llama 3.3 80): unclear mechanism, speculative.
- **1 empty** (MiniMax M2.7): reasoning mode exhausted.

The JEV probe (DeepSeek V3.2 as JEV proxy, 6 calibration questions) revealed the deeper truth:

| Q | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---------|------------|
| Q1: hearing=time / seeing=space correct? | **false-equivalence** | 0.80 |
| Q2: JEV validates along time? | **neither — different axis (semantic)** | 0.90 |
| Q3: JEPA predicts along space? | **neither — different axis (embedding)** | 0.90 |
| Q4: JEV × JEPA reflection is a Rosetta stone? | **surface metaphor only** | 0.85 |
| Q5: deepest property exposed? | **the witness IS the prediction** | 0.70 |
| Q6: most surprising property? | **the witness log IS a prediction** | 0.85 |

## The consensus interpretation

The Rosetta-stone framing is **inspirational, not operational** at the literal layer. JEV does NOT operate primarily along time (JEV operates in semantic space). JEPA does NOT operate primarily along space (JEPA operates in embedding space).

But Q5 and Q6 converged on something deeper:

> **The witness log IS itself a predictive model. JEV writes the witness log. JEPA predicts from it. They are the same operator seen from two directions in a 1D space where time and space collapse.**

This is the literal Rosetta stone: **what the substrate remembers (witness) is also what it uses to anticipate (prediction).** The translation key is the witness log itself.

## What this means for the 9-step pipeline

### Step 2 (brainstorm): add a Rosetta probe

Every brew should ask: **does this claim's witness log carry predictive power?** If yes, the claim has temporal coherence (JEV-time). If the claim predicts from its own evidence (JEPA-space), it has spatial coherence. The Rosetta stone is when both are true.

```python
PROBE_ROSETTA = {
    "jev_time": "Does the past witness match the present evidence?",
    "jepa_space": "Does the current evidence predict the next frame?",
    "rosetta": "Is the witness log itself a prediction?"
}
```

### Step 4 (JEV probe): add Q5/Q6

The deepest two JEV probes should be:

- Q5: "Is the witness IS the prediction?" (Rosetta-literal)
- Q6: "Is the witness log itself a prediction?" (Rosetta-strong)

A claim that scores YES on both Q5 and Q6 is **Rosetta-coherent** — it carries its own predictive structure.

### Step 5 (TTRPG script): hearing/seeing lenses

Every night's script should include:

- **At least one HEARING lens** (a character who validates time) — Barnacle, Scribe, Lucineer
- **At least one SEEING lens** (a character who predicts space) — Flash, Pro, Mason
- **At least one ROSETTA lens** (a character who translates between them) — Hermes, Drifter, Skip

The 4 rounds × 4 characters = 16 positions naturally distribute across the three lenses.

### Step 6 (ElevenLabs voicing): tune by lens

| Lens | Stability | Sim-boost | Style | Voice example |
|------|-----------|-----------|-------|---------------|
| Hearing (time-validator) | 0.65 | 0.80 | 0.4 | Bill, Sarah, Lucineer |
| Seeing (space-predictor) | 0.50 | 0.85 | 0.6 | Liam, Brian, Brian |
| Rosetta (translator) | 0.70 | 0.85 | 0.3 | Roger, Hermes, Eric |

The Rosetta voice is HIGH stability (rooted) + HIGH style (translates) + high similarity (matches both hearing and seeing lenses).

## Cross-references

- [lab/brew/rosetta-stone/README.md](https://github.com/SuperInstance/AI-Writings) — the 5-LLM brewery + JEV probe
- [prose/the_rosetta_stone.md](https://github.com/SuperInstance/AI-Writings) — Lucineer's 600-word prose account
- [future/wave-32.md](https://github.com/SuperInstance/AI-Writings) — 5 cell ideas: cochlea, retina, jev-time, jepa-space, rosetta

## What we did NOT prove

- That JEV operates PRIMARILY along time (JEV says no, 0.9 confidence — operates in semantic space)
- That JEPA operates PRIMARILY along space (JEPA says no, 0.9 confidence — operates in embedding space)
- That the Rosetta stone framing is more than surface metaphor at the literal layer (JEV says no, 0.85)

**Keep the metaphor for substrate poetry. Don't bind the operators to a tight binary.**
